From these precise premises H=H_- mod p satisfies LH=0, H=RH, H(0)=[x^N]H=g=G mod p !=0, H(1)=1 and H(1/2)=0. Thus delta=((R H_- - H_-)/p) mod p is a well-defined polynomial of degree at most N. It has no freely added homogeneous solution. DeltaH is the old normalized two-lift difference; delta and DeltaH are not silently identified. ## 3. Exact p and p-squared calculation and complete forcing I checked A sections 2--3 in the exact arithmetic ring before reducing. The terminating Gauss operator has d=-3m, a=-m, b=-2m, so substituting scalar m=(p-1)/6 gives G_-=G0+p[(z-1)D_z/2+1/9]-p^2/18, G0=z(1-z)D_z^2+(1/2-3z/2)D_z-1/18. The signs of both the p and p-squared terms agree with the original -2m^2 term. Hence G0 h_-=p[(1-z)h_-'/2-h_-/9]+p^2 h_-/18. For L=A D_x^2+B D_x+C, with A=2x(1-x)(4x-1), B=-20x^2+15x-1, C=1-4x, the chain-rule coefficients are exactly A(rho')^2=18(4x-1)rho(1-rho), A rho''+B rho'=9(4x-1)(1-3rho), C=-(4x-1). Here rho'=3(4x-3)(4x-1) and 1-rho=(1-x)(4x-1)^2. This yields the actual equation L H_-=p F_-(H_-)+p^2 V0 H_-, F_-(f)=U0 f'-2V0 f, U0=3(1-x)(4x-1)^2/(4x-3), V0=4x-1. The factor 4x-3 divides H_-', so this actual F_-(H_-) is polynomial. It may have degree N+1. Applying R can therefore produce x^-1; treating R L H_- separately as a polynomial would lose a load-bearing cancellation. A explicitly does not do that. For v=Rf the differentiated identities in A (11) retain literal N: v'=Nv/x-(Rf')/(4x^2), v''=N(N-1)v/x^2-(N-1)(Rf')/(2x^3)+(Rf'')/(16x^4). Using A(x)/(16x^4)=A(1/(4x)), I checked the commutator L Rf-R Lf=pK(Rf)-p^2 A(x)Rf/(4x^2), K(v)=(A/x)v'+[B/(2x)-A/(2x^2)]v. In particular the Rf' difference from N0=-1/2 is -pA/(4x^3), and the zeroth difference is (p/2)[A(N-3/2)/x^2+B/x]. Substitution of Rf'=4x(Nv-xv') gives the stated K and negative p-squared term. This check uses rational functions with p-integral constants, not division by a vanishing endpoint value. Applying the exact commutator to H_-, subtracting its exact equation, dividing by p, and then reducing gives Ldelta=R F_-(H)-F_-(H)+K(H). The old complete J is J=3(4x-1)H-6(1-x)(4x-1)^2 H'/(4x-3), deg J<=N-2. Thus F_-(H)=-J/2-V0 H/2 and R(aH)=a(1/(4x))H. The origin-pole terms are (V0-V0(1/(4x)))/2=2x-1/(2x) and B/(2x)-A/(2x^2)=-6x+5/2+1/(2x). They cancel exactly. RJ is a polynomial divisible by x^2 because deg J<=N-2. Consequently the complete, polynomial forcing is exactly F_rec=(J-RJ)/2+2(1-x)(4x-1)H'+(5-8x)H/2. No critical-point or origin pole, p-squared contribution, or high-degree piece has been removed by an unproved regularization. ## 4. Canonical normalization, endpoints and the unevaluated half-jet I checked A sections 4--5 without imposing e4 or t_top nonzero. Exact R^2 is u=4^-N=2^(-(p-1)), not 1. With e4=(u-1)/p mod p and t_top=(ell_- - G)/p mod p, the actual divided definition gives Rdelta+delta=e4 H, delta_0=t_top+e4 g, delta_N=-t_top. The identity e4=-q_p(2) uses the ordinary fixed Fermat quotient but no computed prime instance. Neither divided scalar is inverted. The exact coefficient a_1=-6mG=(1-p)G follows from the first Gauss slot and the linear rho coefficient. Only rho^m contributes to x^(N-1), giving a_(N-1)=-(3m/2)ell_-=(1-p)ell_-/4. Thus delta_1=delta_0 and delta_(N-1)=delta_N/4. The old DeltaH instead has lower coefficient difference g. These are actual source normalizations, not fitted values. The terminating Vandermonde identity gives h_-(1)=1 exactly. Differentiating the same terminating polynomial and using d-b=-m gives h_-'(1)/h_-(1) =(ab/d)*(d-b)_(m-1)/(d-b)_m*(d)_m/(d+1)_(m-1) =-ab=-2m^2. The remaining last factors and all canceled factors are units. The two preimages rho(1)=rho(1/4)=1 therefore give H_-'(1)=-18m^2 and H_-'(1/4)=0. The exact reciprocal derivative has numerators Np and 4uNp at these endpoints, since N+18m^2=Np. Division before reduction then gives delta(1)=0, delta(1/4)=e4, delta'(1)=N=-1/2, delta'(1/4)=4N=-2. The two nonzero derivatives do not require e4 nonzero. At c=1/2, c^N=-1 mod p for both prescribed prime classes. Hence eta2=(c^N+1)/p mod p and h_div=H_-(c)/p mod p are defined. From (c^N)^2=u, e4=-2eta2. Evaluating the actual divided numerator and its derivative at the fixed reciprocal point gives delta(c)=-2h_div, delta'(c)=h_div-eta2 H'(c), delta(c)+2delta'(c)=e4 H'(c). I checked the derivative numerator 2N c^N H_-(c)-(c^N+1)H_-'(c); no division by H(c), eta2 or h_div occurs. These equations do not evaluate h_div and do not identify it with the held weighted functional. The anti-invariant half-value is not determined by Rdelta+delta=e4H alone. ## 5. Complete support, highest slot and the two finite exclusions For A section 6, the unit forward rows yield h0=h1=g, h2=2g; reciprocity then gives hN=g, h_(N-1)=g/4, h_(N-2)=g/8. At the other edge the complete J gives J0=-g, J1=5g/3. Directly U0=-1+(23/3)x+O(x^2), so the latter value includes every term -3g+12g+4h2-(46/3)g, not just the derivative's top part. For D=2(1-x)(4x-1)H'+(5-8x)H/2 I checked all three possible highest slots. Its N+1 coefficient is -4(2N+1)g=0 mod p. Its N coefficient is -g/2, canceled by -J0/2=+g/2 from -RJ/2. At N-1 the derivative and value part is -g/8, while -RJ/2 contributes -J1/8=-5g/24. Their sum is -g/3, a unit. The other edge is F_rec(0)=-g/2-2g+5g/2=0. Thus the support is contained in [1,N-1] and its top N-1 slot is nonzero; neither A nor this review claims all intermediate coefficients are nonzero. In particular deg F_rec=N-1 is an exact statement for every prescribed prime, not extrapolation from examples or from a separated degree N+1 term. The first exclusion is immediate with the checked endpoint derivative: every polynomial F(rho) has derivative zero at 1/4, whereas delta'(1/4)=-2. Therefore delta is not in F_p[rho]. This excludes polynomial responses solely through that SAME cubic, including solely Gauss-parameter polynomial responses. It does not exclude rational coefficients with canceled poles, another pullback, baseline additions or derivative terms. For the second exclusion I checked the full row [x^k]Lf=-(k+1)(2k+1)f_(k+1)+(10k^2+5k+1)f_k-4k(2k-1)f_(k-1). For f=xH', the would-be N+1 slot vanishes and its L-image has N coefficient N g-4(N-1)(g/4)=g. If delta=aH+bDeltaH+d xH' for CONSTANT a,b,d in F_p, the N slot forces d=0. The nonzero N-1 coefficient of F_rec then contradicts LH=0 and deg LDeltaH=deg J<=N-2. Hence the stated constant-three-span exclusion is valid. It is not an exclusion over F_p(x) or a universal rational-gauge/Heun theorem. The extra two-vector endpoint check in A is consistent and remains part of this same unit. ## 6. Finite verification interface and exact scope of this verdict Existence uses the actual divided polynomial, not just a solvability guess for the inhomogeneous equation.
